fill_instructions.checkpoint_id: Allocate the next six-digit checkpoint sequence for this work item and append eight lowercase hex characters from a newly generated UUID. Do not derive control authority from the identifier.
fill_instructions.created_at: Record the current UTC RFC3339 timestamp from an authoritative time source at checkpoint creation.
fill_instructions.source_main_sha: Freshly read the authorized repository default-branch head immediately before checkpoint creation and record the exact 40-hex SHA.
fill_instructions.work_identity: Read the work record and implementation branch. Record work_id, work_branch, and the branch head SHA actually observed. If there is no work item, use null only where the checkpoint schema permits null; do not invent an identity.
fill_instructions.trigger_ids: Evaluate every checkpoint-policy trigger using exact states/counters/timestamps. Record every trigger that is true at creation. Do not add a trigger because it seems important.
fill_instructions.previous_checkpoint: If a prior checkpoint exists for this work item, record its repository path and Git blob SHA. Otherwise record null values as allowed by schema. Never store the current checkpoint's own hash inside itself.
fill_instructions.selected_work: Run the deterministic selector against the current required evidence and record its observed lane/rank/selection. This is historical evidence only; a future thread must select again after fresh live verification.
fill_instructions.canonical_snapshot: Record current repository continuity fields and the exact mismatch/blocker ID sets observed at creation. Do not rewrite UNKNOWN, NOT_RUN, UNVERIFIED, or INFERRED as VERIFIED.
fill_instructions.claim_observations: Freshly read every claim relevant to the current work item or selected work. Record resource key, lock branch, ownership fields, state, expiry, observed_at, and live_verify_required=true. A stored claim observation never proves future ownership.
fill_instructions.operation_results: For each mutation or interrupted operation since the previous checkpoint, record system, target, operation, exact result state, readback state, and evidence references. A mutation is not VERIFIED unless authoritative readback succeeded.
fill_instructions.directive_refs: Before checkpoint completion, append any new Vince directive/correction intended to survive the thread to continuity/directive-ledger.jsonl with the direct quote and context, then reference its VD identifier here.
fill_instructions.decision_rationale_refs: Reference rationale records that explain architecture selections, alternatives, research, limitations, or reevaluation conditions changed since the previous checkpoint.
fill_instructions.research_refs: When fresh research changed or confirmed a persistent mechanism, record source kind, title, canonical URL, observation date, and the exact claim it supports. Do not cite research that was not actually consulted.
fill_instructions.live_verify: List every volatile GitHub, Supabase, or Vercel object on which the resume candidate depends. A future thread must reread these objects before using the checkpoint to continue work.
fill_instructions.resume_candidate: Describe the exact interrupted or next candidate operation and its last observed operation state. Set authority to NONE. It is not an authorization, priority decision, or mutation permission; bootstrap plus live verification plus deterministic selection must run first.
fill_instructions.context_refs: Reference repository artifacts needed to understand surrounding rationale, including directive/rationale IDs, PRs, issues, commits, workflow runs, or research sources. Prefer exact identifiers over narrative summaries.
fill_instructions.completion: Write the checkpoint as canonical JSON, read it back from GitHub, and record the returned blob identity externally in the next checkpoint or Git history. Do not claim checkpoint completion when write or readback is NO_RESULT, TIMEOUT, UNKNOWN, or FAILURE.
